survey: A white, ball-shaped astronaut helmet faces the camera at three-quarter view and sits on a sci-fi shelf. Main parts: (1) A spherical white shell. It looks round and even, with no dents or warping. (2) A large oval yellow visor set into the front of the shell, with glossy reflections. (3) A silver tube-like rim around the visor, set flush into the shell. (4) A neck ring under the shell: a silver collar band on top of a white cylinder with a red stripe. The helmet's bottom edge sits down into the silver collar, so it reads as attached. (5) The neck ring stands flat on a light grey metal shelf with small rivets. Its base touches the shelf and casts a contact shadow, so nothing floats. Counts are right: one visor, one rim, one neck ring. There are no loose cables, invented glows or extra parts. A helmet resting on its neck ring is a believable display pose.

errors.where: Silver visor rim, right side, at about the 3 o'clock position
errors.what: The rim is not one closed loop. There is a visible step where its two ends meet slightly out of line, like a ring that has been cut and its ends overlapped. A sealed helmet visor frame should be continuous.

fix: Make the silver visor rim one smooth, continuous closed oval band of even thickness all the way around, with no seam, step or overlapping ends on the right side.
